about: The City of Fort Walton Beach calls the Downtown Holiday Market and Light Up the Night Tree Lighting one of the most festive and magical events of the year. It takes place on Saturday, November 28, 2026, from 11 AM to 6 PM at the Landing in downtown, brought to you by Eglin Federal Credit Union.

The city promises more than 100 local vendors selling handmade goods, locally sourced products and gifts, plus live music through the day, food trucks and cookie decorating. Santa and Mrs. Claus make an appearance.

The Landing has all new Christmas displays this year, with new lighting, a new tree and a Santa's Workshop. At the end of the day the Fort Walton Beach Community Chorus carols during the countdown to the tree lighting, which is set for 5:30 PM prompt.
The Landing is at 131 Brooks Street SE, Fort Walton Beach 32548. The city page does not mention an admission price, so plan on shopping and food truck costs only.
Because the market opens at 11 AM and the tree lights at 5:30 PM, families with little ones can visit for the cookies and Santa in the afternoon and come back for the lighting.
faq: When is the Fort Walton Beach tree lighting 2026?
Saturday, November 28, 2026, at 5:30 PM, during a market from 11 AM to 6 PM.

about: The Island Resort and Convention Center lists A Beachy Little Christmas on Saturday, December 12, 2026, from noon to 4 PM. The resort calls it a festive afternoon of holiday fun by the water, with a little coastal twist.

Guests meet Santa Claus and Misty the Mermaid for special photo opportunities, then get creative with Christmas themed sandcastle building. The resort's event page says it is free and open to the public.
The page names the Beach as the location. It does not print a street address, a parking note or an age guide, so check the resort's calendar before you go.
A beach event suits families who want a casual, sandy alternative to an evening parade, and the midday hours work well for naps and early bedtimes.

The resort publishes the event on its calendar of events for Fort Walton Beach, where its page also lists the activities as photos with Santa Claus and Misty the Mermaid and Christmas themed sandcastle building.

site: Giveaways of toys, bikes and presents

about: United for a Good Cause hosts the Emerald Coast Christmas Miracle Fiesta on Sunday, December 20, 2026, from noon to 6 PM at the Fort Walton Beach Recreation Center, 132 Jet Drive. The group describes it as a free Christmas fiesta where every child goes home with a gift.

The first hour, noon to 1 PM, is open only to families of children with special needs so they can enjoy the fiesta at a calmer pace. Everyone is welcome from 1 PM, regardless of race, ethnicity or creed.

Every December, families from across the region come together for the fiesta, which includes entertainment, food, tables run by partner agencies, and hundreds of toys, bikes and presents. Families can register ahead, and families who did not register can still walk in and may win a bike through the games.
The organization's page gives no age range other than every child, so ask the group about older kids and teens before you go.

about: The Okaloosa County Public Library Cooperative lists a Christmas Party with Santa at the Fort Walton Beach Library on Thursday, December 10, 2026, from 5 PM to 7 PM. The listing marks it a drop in event for all ages, with no registration required.
Santa will read a story, and children will then have a chance to take photos with him. The library also plans gingerbread house judging, crafts and hot cocoa.
The audience tags on the listing span babies through teens, so it works for mixed age families. The listing does not print a price or a street address, so check the library's page for directions.
Because it runs on a weeknight evening, families can come straight from school or work and stay for the story.

The Okaloosa County Public Library Cooperative runs a shared event calendar for its branches, so families can look up other December programs from the same page. Santa's reading is the cue for children to gather before photos start.
